subject: RFP: Operational contacts, on-call coverage & incident notification SLAs

Subject: RFP section — support & on-call specifics (clarifications requested)

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the submission so far — we're working through the vendor responses and have a few follow-ups specifically around the Support & CS section. Can you confirm the following items for inclusion in our SOW/RFP evaluation?

1) On-call coverage: do you provide a 24x7 primary on-call for production incidents for enterprise Dedicated/Private customers, or is that an add-on? If so, what's the typical escalation chain (T1/T2/T3) and expected response SLA at each level?

2) Notification channels: we need to know your supported channels for urgent incidents (PagerDuty, email, SMS, phone). Do you support direct escalation to our SOC via PagerDuty integration?

3) Incident comms cadence: for Sev 1 and Sev 2 incidents, what is your standard cadence for acknowledgement, updates, and postmortem delivery? Include target windows.

4) Roster visibility: can you provide a machine-readable on-call roster or API for our SREs to integrate?

5) Runbooks & playbooks: are these available prior to go-live, and will you provide contact-level details in the documentation (roles, escalation timeouts)?

If you could return a concise table or the attached RFP template filled out it would be ideal. We may request a short follow-up call to walk through any atypical items.

Best,
Aisha Malik
Senior Procurement Manager
Finovate Financial Services

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear questions. Please find answers inline below and the completed RFP_Support_Questions_Filled.xlsx attached. I'll also attach our Oncall_Rotation_SLA_Overview.pdf for the high-level SLAs. Short answers first, then details.

1) On-call coverage
- Short: 24x7 primary coverage is included for Dedicated customers on enterprise plans; for Private/on-prem we offer an add-on managed on-call service.
- Details: For Dedicated (enterprise tier) customers we staff a regional on-call rotation that provides a named primary engineer during the active window; the rotation supports global handoff for customers requiring 24x7. For Private deployments we can provide the same staffed coverage under a managed-services agreement (typically +20% of base fee).

2) Notification channels
- We support PagerDuty and can integrate with your existing routing via the API (Key-based integration), as well as email, SMS, and phone escalation. Direct escalation to customer SOC via PagerDuty is supported and commonly used.

3) Incident comms cadence
- Sev 1: Acknowledgement target = 15 minutes; status updates every 30 minutes until mitigated; preliminary RCA within 72 hours, full postmortem within 14 calendar days.
- Sev 2: Acknowledgement target = 60 minutes; updates every 4 hours; root cause analysis within 7 business days.

4) Roster visibility
- We provide a read-only API endpoint and an optional PagerDuty roster export that your SREs can poll. We can also provide an LDAP/SCIM integration for enterprise customers for identity mapping.

5) Runbooks & playbooks
- We provide customer-specific operational runbooks during onboarding (locked to the deployment model and network topology). Contact-level details (roles and escalation timeouts) are included in those runbooks and kept current during manual rotation changes.

Attachments: RFP_Support_Questions_Filled.xlsx (completed table); Oncall_Rotation_SLA_Overview.pdf (summary).

If helpful, Marissa (cc'd) can share a sanitized example runbook for a bank deploy. We are available for a 30-min review call late this week or early next week.

Thanks,

Hi Aisha — adding operational detail on escalation timeline and example contact flow so you can paste into your SOW language.

Quoted for context:
On Fri, Nov 12, 2026 at 13:27 Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> 1) On-call coverage
> - Short: 24x7 primary coverage is included for Dedicated customers on enterprise plans; for Private/on-prem we offer an add-on managed on-call service.

Operational escalation chain (example):
- Triage (T1): Customer-reported + automated alert intake — initial on-call engineer. Response target: 15 minutes (Sev1) / 60 minutes (Sev2).
- Engineering escalation (T2): If not mitigated within 30 minutes for Sev1 or 4 hours for Sev2, ticket escalates to senior on-call who has write access to deployment. Response target: 30 minutes.
- Product/Platform escalation (T3): For complex kernel/runtime issues or cross-region failover, engineering director on-call engaged; typical response target 2 hours.

Out-of-band communications and executive briefings:
- For Sev1 impacting production capacity > 30 minutes we trigger an executive notification (email + phone call) to named contacts in the SLA.
- We maintain an incident Slack bridge or secure Zoom room for high-severity incidents.

Runbook maintenance and access:
- Customer runbooks are versioned in our secured Confluence space and exports provided on request. We can redact internal-only procedures for a sanitized copy for RFP inclusion.

Data retention & audit trails:
- Incident timelines, on-call handover logs, and postmortem are retained for 12 months by default; extended retention is available as an add-on with encryption-at-rest assured.

I can provide suggested SOW language if that helps procurement.

—Marissa
Head of Technical Customer Success
redwoodinference.com

Attachment referenced: example_sanitized_runbook_sample.pdf (we will provide on request)
